old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a steaming cup of coffee, held by a hand. The cup is glass with a reflective surface, and the coffee inside is dark and rich, with a layer of froth on top. Steam rises gently from the coffee, indicating its warmth. The background is blurred, drawing attention to the cup and the steam. The lighting is soft but bright enough to highlight the details of the coffee and the cup's texture. The cup remains static throughout the sequence. The overall atmosphere is cozy and inviting, emphasizing the comforting nature of the hot beverage.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a steaming cup of coffee, held by a hand. The cup is metallic with a reflective surface, and the coffee inside is dark and rich, with a layer of froth on top. Steam rises gently from the coffee, indicating its warmth. The background is blurred, drawing attention to the cup and the steam. The lighting is soft but bright enough to highlight the details of the coffee and the cup's texture. As the video progresses, there is a subtle shift in the angle of the cup, suggesting a slight movement of the hand holding it. The overall atmosphere is cozy and inviting, emphasizing the comforting nature of the hot beverage.
caption: The video captures a tight close-up of a transparent glass mug with a handle on the left, held by bare fingers and filled nearly to the brim with a dark hot beverage. A bright out-of-focus light glows upper-left, throwing a lens flare and a greenish-blue circular artifact across the liquid surface against a dark background. Wisps of steam are already rising from the drink. A faint puff drifting up from the rim center thickens into a vertical column, then thins and tilts leftward toward the light before dispersing. New wisps reappear and continue curling upward and sideways, showing steady, unbroken evaporation. The liquid surface shimmers with shifting micro-texture, yet the fill level and rim position stay constant. The hand, mug, and green flare remain fixed, so all apparent motion comes from the rising steam.
